Day of Remembrance of the Quebec City Mosque attack. The City of Kitchener joins Canadians
across Canada in reflecting on this National Day of Remembrance of the Quebec City Mosque
attack in action against Islamophobia. We condemn the senseless attack at the Centre
Cultural Islamique de Québec and commit to the collective fight to end Islamophobia.
Seven years ago today, Muslim worshippers at the Islamic Cultural Centre of Quebec City
were subjected to a tragic and hateful gunman attack that left six men dead,
19 people injured, some permanently disabled, and many more severely traumatized.
Today, Kitchener joins cities and communities across Canada to take a moment of silence
to remember Ibrahemi Berry, Mamadou Tanu Berry, Khaled Belkachemi, Abdulkrem Hassane,
Azdin Sufiona, and Abu Bakr Thabti. Unfortunately, this Islamophobic act is one of many examples we
have witnessed across our nation and here in Waterloo Region. Closer to home, we remember
the disturbing vehicle attack in London, Ontario in 2021 that killed Madea Salman,
Yumna Avsal, Salman Avsal and Talat Avsal and left their son, Fayez Avsal, injured and orphaned.
In the Coalition of Muslim Women KW's second annual snapshot of hate in Waterloo Region report,
97 unique incidents of hate or racial discrimination were recorded and of that,
53 percent were identified as being against Muslims. These incidents took place in
in institutions, retail stores, neighbourhoods and online.
Canada has the highest number of deaths related to Islamophobia in all G7 countries.
We are seeing a significant spike in Islamophobia across Canada, especially in the last few
months.
And it's imperative that we address this hate proactively and mitigate the harm before
it spreads even further.
This week, across Canada, communities are standing together in unity with our Muslim
neighbours by lighting buildings and infrastructure in green lights, as we are last night and
this evening here at City Hall, lowering flags to half-mast, providing supportive messages
on signage boards and joining in the National Green Square Campaign, which is organised
by the National Council of Canadian Muslims and others.
In Kitchener, Carls-Hair Square at City Hall has been lit green and our flags are at half-mast.
All City of Kitchener community centres with digital signs are also displaying messages
of support for the Green Square campaign.
This campaign represents the green carpets of Centre Cultural Islamique du Québec, the
last place where the victim stood to pray.
It also symbolizes the Islamic belief that the lost lives are in a green garden, a better
place.
I call on Kitchener residents to join us to stand with those working to eliminate Islamophobia,
hate and racism in Canada by participating in the Green Square campaign.
Islamophobia and religious hate have no place in Kitchener, in Canada or anywhere.
No one should be discriminated against based on their religion.
Today we stand in solidarity with our local Muslim community as we remember victims of
the Islamophobic attack in Quebec City and across Ontario and Canada.
We also thank local leaders such as those with the Coalition of Muslim Women KW, Muslim
Social Services of Kitchener-Waterloo, the Muslim Association of Canada, the Maple Grove
School and others who work tirelessly every day to educate our community and combat Islamophobia
throughout Kitchener and Waterloo Region.
I'd now like us to stand as we're able to reflect through a moment of silence.
Thank you.
